classification.difficultyReason: Identify the single-toss probabilities and multiply across three independent tosses. The hardest interpretation is that 'the first two tosses only' requires 6, 6, then not 6; each part otherwise specifies one ordered path using the taught method.

content.prompt: A die is tossed three times. What is the probability of obtaining:

answer.worked:
The tosses are independent, and the probability of a 6 on each toss is $\frac{1}{6}$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{three 6s})&=\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{1}{6}\\P(\text{three 6s})&=\frac{1}{216}\end{align*}$$

The probability of not obtaining a 6 on each independent toss is $\frac{5}{6}$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{no 6s})&=\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{5}{6}\\P(\text{no 6s})&=\frac{125}{216}\end{align*}$$

The odd outcomes are $1,3,5$, so the probability of an odd number on each independent toss is $\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{three odd numbers})&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\\P(\text{three odd numbers})&=\frac{1}{8}\end{align*}$$

The even outcomes are $2,4,6$, so the probability of an even number on each independent toss is $\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{three even numbers})&=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\\P(\text{three even numbers})&=\frac{1}{8}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: a 6 in the first two tosses only?

answer.worked:
The required order is 6, 6, then not a 6. Multiply the probabilities of these independent outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{6, 6, not 6})&=\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{5}{6}\\P(\text{6, 6, not 6})&=\frac{5}{216}\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: a 6, not a 6, and a 6 in that order?

answer.worked:
Multiply the probabilities in the specified order; the tosses are independent.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{6, not 6, 6})&=\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{1}{6}\\P(\text{6, not 6, 6})&=\frac{5}{216}\end{align*}$$
